applied.problem: "The turn that done twice lands on −1 is the quarter turn" says the quarter turn is the only one, but the next sentence shows 270° done twice lands on −1 too; on the handle two turns do it, and 90° is the smaller.
"which is why −1 × −1 = 1" makes the turning picture the reason for the rule; the picture fits the rule Dan met in Negative numbers but does not prove it, so it should say the two agree.
The last common mistake says "a turn splits into two equal quarter turns"; it is a half turn that splits into two quarter turns (a full turn would split into two half turns).
